# LB5 / 5th Place — Gap analysis (us vs the 5th-place writeup)

> "our approach" cites `competitions/nvidia-nemotron/{notes,submissions,tracking,insights,equation-frontier,bugs}.md`.
> "writeup" cites `../writeup/lb5-writeup.md` (= `temp/LB5.pdf`). `unknown` where the repo records nothing.
> Our best: **soup (v14+c1+b1) Public 0.86 / Private 0.85**; post-deadline **eq-aug 0.86/0.86**. LB5: **Private 0.900** (best, unselected; chosen 0.896). Gap ≈ +0.05 private — and LB5 got there **without solving cryptarithm**.

## Why our EQ1..EQ4 / T12 / replay / synthetic / merge attempts did not close the gap
- **EQ1..EQ4:** We treated equation as a **global cipher**; LB5's per-prompt 2-world/4-family/13-rule solver hits **~96%** — the **third independent refutation** (LB1 95%, LB3 93%, LB5 96%). The deduce subset is per-prompt operators; re-test (no GPU).
- **T12 hard-val:** Late, atypical-adapter-fragile, and optimized against the **public** LB. LB5's no-leakage CV is a more honest, private-tracking signal.
- **replay (v14):** Generic ceiling lever; doesn't solve bit/equation/cryptarithm structurally.
- **synthetic (b1/b2/v15/c1/c2):** Too small + diluting. LB5 generates the **entire** training set statistics-matched (no leakage), the opposite of bolt-on.
- **merge/soup (0.86):** Our soup is **one-shot**. LB5 shows the larger win is **iterative LoRA averaging as a training-time regularizer** (stability across 15 iterations), turning an unstable 0.87 into a stable 0.90.

## High-value vs not-worth-it (for future competitions)
**High value (do):** **iterative LoRA averaging / multi-seed soup** as a training regularizer (not just one-shot); a **no-leakage synthetic generator → private-tracking CV**; **ternary byte-level bit solver** with memorized continuations; **cut to ~7 examples** for budget; multi-round high-LR SFT (no forgetting); **full logical CoT** (short/guess CoT fails); re-test the equation-deduce premise.
**Too expensive / not worth (skip):** GRPO/pseudo-GRPO on Kaggle (air-gapped, failed); Unsloth 4-bit + packing (breaks Nemotron); DoRA (vLLM unsupported); token-saving **encodings that merge into single tokens** (broke the model); chasing the **public** LB (it plateaued while private rose). **Note:** unlike LB1/LB3, LB5 shows you can reach 0.90 **without** cryptarithm — but cryptarithm is the 0.90→0.92 lever, so it's worth it only if aiming for the very top.
